title: Tangents and the Derivative at a Point
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Derivative of a Function at a Point
definitions.latex: f'(x_0) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x_0 + h) - f(x_0)}{h} = \lim_{z \to x_0} \frac{f(z) - f(x_0)}{z - x_0}
definitions.statement: The derivative of a function f at a point x0 is the limit of the difference quotient as h approaches zero, provided this limit exists.
conditions: f is defined in an open interval containing x0
The limit is a finite real number
definitions.explanation: Represents both the slope of the tangent line to y = f(x) at (x0, f(x0)) and the instantaneous rate of change of y with respect to x at x0.
definitions.keyTakeaway: f'(x0) is the instantaneous rate of change and the tangent slope at x0.

definitions.title: Tangent and Normal Line Equations
definitions.latex: \text{Tangent: } y - y_0 = f'(x_0)(x - x_0), \qquad \text{Normal: } y - y_0 = -\frac{1}{f'(x_0)}(x - x_0) \quad (f'(x_0) \neq 0)
definitions.statement: The tangent line passes through (x0, y0) with slope f'(x0). The normal line is perpendicular to the tangent line at the point of tangency.
conditions: f'(x0) exists and is non-zero for normal line
If f'(x0) = 0, tangent is horizontal y = y0 and normal is vertical x = x0
definitions.explanation: Perpendicular lines in the Cartesian plane have negative reciprocal slopes: m1 * m2 = -1.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Normal line slope is the negative reciprocal of tangent slope.
